subject: HIN
label: Grade 02
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 02 Hindi, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Family and home words
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Family and home words', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: name family members. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Family and home words' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: name family members, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Maa (mother), pitaji (father), bhai (brother), behan (sister). 'Yeh mera ghar hai.' (This is my home.) Method: Model run for 'Family and home words'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Name family members: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Learn family words: माँ [mother], पिताजी [father], भाई [brother], बहन [sister], दादा [paternal grandfather], दादी [paternal grandmother], नाना [maternal grandfather], नानी [maternal grandmother], चाचा [paternal uncle]. Say each word and point to a family photo.

Step 2, Use मेरा, मेरी, मेरे [my]. मेरा भाई [my brother], मेरी बहन [my sister], मेरी माँ [my mother], मेरे पिताजी [my father]. Match with the noun: मेरा for a masculine noun, मेरी for a feminine noun, मेरे for a respectful or plural one.

Step 3, Introduce people. यह मेरी माँ हैं। [This is my mother.] ये मेरे दादाजी हैं। [This is my grandfather.] यह मेरा भाई है। [This is my brother.] वह मेरी बहन है। [That is my sister.] Elders take हैं as a mark of respect.

Step 4, Ask and answer. तुम्हारे घर में कौन-कौन है? [Who is in your house?] मेरे घर में माँ, पिताजी, दादी और मैं हैं। [In my house there are mother, father, grandmother and I.] घर में चार लोग हैं। [There are four people in the house.]
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says मेरा बहन. Correction: मेरी बहन, because बहन is feminine. Another slip is मेरी भाई; say मेरा भाई. Look at the noun first, then pick मेरा or मेरी.

Step 6, Your turn: write three sentences introducing your mother, brother and grandmother. Model answer: यह मेरी माँ हैं। यह मेरा भाई है। ये मेरी दादी हैं। [This is my mother. This is my brother. This is my grandmother.]

modules.title: Colours and numbers
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Colours and numbers', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: name colours and numbers to 20. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Colours and numbers' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: name colours and numbers to 20, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: lal (red), neela (blue), hara (green). ek, do, teen are 1, 2, 3. Method: Model run for 'Colours and numbers'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Name colours and numbers to 20: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Learn colours: लाल [red], नीला [blue], हरा [green], पीला [yellow], सफ़ेद [white], काला [black], गुलाबी [pink], नारंगी [orange]. Hold up crayons and ask: यह कौन-सा रंग है? [Which colour is this?] Answer: यह लाल है। [This is red.]
Step 2, Count from 1 to 10: एक, दो, तीन, चार, पाँच, छह, सात, आठ, नौ, दस. Then 11 to 20: ग्यारह, बारह, तेरह, चौदह, पंद्रह, सोलह, सत्रह, अठारह, उन्नीस, बीस. Count marbles, and say each number aloud.

Step 3, Make sentences. मेरे पास पाँच लाल गुब्बारे हैं। [I have five red balloons.] टोकरी में बारह आम हैं। [There are twelve mangoes in the basket.] आसमान नीला है। [The sky is blue.] Count and describe objects around you.

Step 4, Match colour words to the noun. हरा तोता [a green parrot], हरी मिर्च [a green chilli], हरे पत्ते [green leaves]. Colours ending in आ change: हरा for a masculine noun, हरी for a feminine noun, हरे for a plural masculine noun.
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says हरा मिर्च. Correction: हरी मिर्च, because मिर्च is feminine. Also सत्रह is the number for 17 and अठारह is 18; keep the two apart by listening to the middle sound.

Step 6, Your turn: say you have fifteen yellow flowers and a blue bag. Model answer: मेरे पास पंद्रह पीले फूल हैं। मेरा बस्ता नीला है। [I have fifteen yellow flowers. My bag is blue.] Notice पीले agrees with the plural फूल.

modules.title: Animals and birds
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Animals and birds', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: name animals and birds. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Animals and birds' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: name animals and birds, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: kutta (dog), billi (cat), tota (parrot), mor (peacock). 'Yeh tota hai.' (This is a parrot.) Method: Model run for 'Animals and birds'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Name animals and birds: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Name animals: शेर [lion], हाथी [elephant], बंदर [monkey], गाय [cow], कुत्ता [dog], बिल्ली [cat]. Then birds: तोता [parrot], मोर [peacock], कौआ [crow], चिड़िया [sparrow], कबूतर [pigeon]. Say each word and imitate the creature.

Step 2, Describe them in short sentences. हाथी बड़ा है। [The elephant is big.] तोता हरा है। [The parrot is green.] बिल्ली छोटी है। [The cat is small.] शेर दहाड़ता है। [The lion roars.] Notice बड़ा, छोटी change with the noun.

Step 3, Say what animals do. गाय दूध देती है। [The cow gives milk.] कौआ काँव-काँव करता है। [The crow caws.] मोर नाचता है। [The peacock dances.] चिड़िया पेड़ पर बैठी है। [The sparrow is sitting on the tree.]
Step 4, Ask and answer. तुम्हें कौन-सा जानवर पसंद है? [Which animal do you like?] मुझे हाथी पसंद है। [I like the elephant.] क्यों? [Why?] क्योंकि वह बहुत बड़ा है। [Because he is very big.]
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says तोता बैठी है. Correction: तोता बैठा है, because तोता is masculine. Likewise say चिड़िया बैठी है, because चिड़िया is feminine, not चिड़िया बैठा है.
Step 6, Your turn: write about a peacock and a cat. Model answer: मोर सुंदर है। वह नाचता है। बिल्ली छोटी है। वह दूध पीती है। [The peacock is beautiful. It dances. The cat is small. It drinks milk.]

modules.title: Short sentences
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Short sentences', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: read and write short sentences. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Short sentences' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: read and write short sentences, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: मेरा नाम अमन है। मैं स्कूल जाता हूँ। यह मेरी किताब है। शब्द: कलम, किताब, गेंद। Method: Model run for 'Short sentences'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Read and write short sentences: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Learn the order of a Hindi sentence: who, what, action. मीना किताब पढ़ती है। [Meena reads a book.] Here मीना is the doer, किताब is the thing, पढ़ती है is the action. The action comes at the end.

Step 2, Make more sentences. रवि फुटबॉल खेलता है। [Ravi plays football.] माँ रोटी बनाती है। [Mother makes roti.] मैं पानी पीता हूँ। [I drink water, said by a boy.] मैं पानी पीती हूँ। [I drink water, said by a girl.]

Step 3, End sentences correctly. A full stop in Hindi is a vertical line। not a dot. Write: बच्चे स्कूल जाते हैं। [Children go to school.] Check that every sentence ends with the vertical line, and leave a space between words.

Step 4, Describe a picture. चित्र में एक लड़की है। [In the picture there is a girl.] वह फूल तोड़ती है। [She picks a flower.] पास में एक कुत्ता है। [Nearby there is a dog.] वह भौंकता है। [He barks.] Look at each picture and say three sentences.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes पढ़ती मीना किताब है. Correction: मीना किताब पढ़ती है। The action word should be at the end. Also check that the verb matches the doer: लड़का खेलता है, लड़की खेलती है.
Step 6, Your turn: write two sentences about a boy who drinks milk and a girl who reads. Model answer: लड़का दूध पीता है। लड़की किताब पढ़ती है। [The boy drinks milk. The girl reads a book.]

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Family and home words), and at which Bloom level is it?
'name', at the Remember level. (Covered in unit 1: Family and home words.)
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36. (Covered in: Assessment plan, near the top of this page.)
In which weeks does Unit 4 (Short sentences) run?
Weeks 28 to 36. (Covered in unit 4: Short sentences.)
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
One page in your learning book. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard. (Covered in: How you are checked, further down this page.)
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
